one_liner: Archived plan for emulated FP64 on Apple GPUs in Metal; no arithmetic is implemented, only theoretical peaks versus CPU FP64.
what_it_does: Aims to give Metal Shading Language a usable 'double' on Apple GPUs, which have no hardware FP64: a macro redefines double/double2-4 to library types, small operations would be inlined and large ones (division, sqrt, transcendentals) called from a Metal dynamic library, and a companion MetalAtomic64 library would emulate 64-bit atomics with a lock buffer. At HEAD the code is only scaffolding: float64_t, float59_t and float43_t are empty wrappers around a ulong with no operators, the only MetalFloat64 source is a placeholder increment(uint) marked 'TODO: Remove this entire file', and the float32x2_t double-single type the README describes does not exist in the sources.
how_it_is_fast: The intended speed comes from emulating FP64 with FP32 and 32-bit integer ALU instructions on the GPU's wide FP32 units: an IEEE path modeled on Berkeley SoftFloat and LLVM compiler-rt fp_lib.h, and a faster double-single (float-float, e8m48) path with flushed denormals. The README's speedups over the CPU's NEON FP64 are instruction-count estimates (for example 11 FP32/integer instructions per double-single add, 7 per multiply), multiplied by the GPU's ALU count and clock; none of that arithmetic is in the repository.
when_to_use: As a design reference when planning your own FP64 or double-single emulation in Metal: the README lists per-operation instruction counts and the dylib-versus-inline split.

As a starting point for lock-buffer 64-bit atomics on Apple GPUs (MetalAtomic64 hashes addresses into a lock buffer, borrowing the idea from Kokkos desul's Lock_Array), after finishing and testing it yourself.
Not for production numerics in any form: there is no working FP64 add, multiply or FMA to call.
when_not_to_use: Any real workload: the README opens with 'Still in the planning stage - this is not a finished library!' and the sources confirm it.
Arbitrary-precision or big-integer work: it is fixed 64-bit floating point, not a GMP or MPFR alternative, so it is in the wrong category for that comparison.

Code that needs correct 64-bit atomics: __metal_atomic64_fetch_add_explicit ignores its type argument and always does integer addition (so f64 adds would be wrong), and the device-memory store has its lock acquire and release left as comments.
Pre-Metal 3 hardware: it needs function pointers and Metal dynamic libraries, so Apple6-family GPUs (A13 and later) or macOS 13 Ventura on Intel Macs.
Fast-math builds of double-single code: the author notes in openmm/openmm#3889 that the Metal compiler optimizes away double-single FP64 emulation.

integration.dependencies: Xcode Metal toolchain (xcrun metal), Swift 5.7 (SwiftPM) for build.swift and the MetalAtomic64 product
integration.min_toolchain: Swift tools 5.7; macOS 13, iOS 16 or tvOS 16 (Package.swift); Metal 3 feature set
integration.platforms: Apple GPUs of the Apple6 family or newer (A13 Bionic and later, Apple silicon Macs); Intel Macs on macOS Ventura
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the 64-bit atomics are the only concurrency code and are incomplete

gotchas: The README warns that forgetting useResource(_:usage:) on the atomics lock buffer can freeze half of the GPU until a restart, or silently draw half its maximum TDP in the background.
The library header copies parts of Apple's Metal Standard Library and says Apple owns the copyright of that code, so the MIT license does not cover all of it.
README and code disagree: the README documents float64_t and float32x2_t, while the headers define float64_t, float59_t and float43_t, and the atomics enum adds f32x2 and f32.
Clients must ship libMetalFloat64.metallib in the same directory as their own library, because it is linked with @loader_path.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Do not pick it for computation: sibling entries such as MultiFloats.hpp, DoubleFloats.jl or libQD3 ship working double-double arithmetic with measurements, while this repository has none. It is only worth reading if you target Metal, which none of the siblings do, and plan to write the emulation yourself.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing was measured: the README table gives theoretical scalar Gops for an unnamed reference system (8-core 3.064 GHz ARM CPU and 32-core 1.296 GHz Apple GPU), derived from instruction counts, comparing CPU hardware FP64 with GPU double-single FP32x2 (e.g. FMUL 196 vs 758, FADD 196 vs 482). The IEEE eFP64 column is empty, most of the precision table is '???', and the code that would produce those numbers does not exist in the repository.
status_note: Archived and read-only since 2024-08-11 with the last commit on 2023-05-17; MIT-licensed but unusable as shipped, since it contains only type scaffolding, a placeholder function and partial 64-bit atomics.
